summary: This article explains how solar ovens use black surfaces, clear lids, and shiny reflectors to cook with sunlight, and why smoke-free cooking matters for the health of millions of families.
introduce: Read the title “Solar Ovens and Clean Cooking” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: to take in or soak up something, such as light, heat, or water
material that stops heat, cold, or sound from passing through
a shiny surface that bounces light back

challengeTerms.def: curved like a bowl in a special shape that sends rays toward one point
to gather or focus something into one small area
having to do with breathing and the lungs

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that every home in a sunny country should own a solar oven? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how the three main parts of a box oven work together to cook food.
struggling: Pre-teach absorb, insulation, and reflector with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use parabolic, concentrate, and respiratory in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
